searchText: I don't see any. So I just made this PR with a couple: * https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5720 I wonder what other edge cases can there be most likely with balances and very minor with forkchoice I guess as we discussed earlier, the report is valid, and I think your fix is the simplest way to solve this and looks correct to me, didn't find anything wrong with it or unwanted side effects <@1557217203034521660> did you by chance use lodestar in your five-node network? BTW, I wonder not only about STF that the tests will cover but block production, I added a unit test to check that Prysm will actually not produce such a block with both slashings. so you are saying we should add spec tests for block production? And there's a few more edge cases that came for this when proposing: actually Prysm has a bug here, if there's a slashing in the pool for a validator that will withdraw, when we miss the cache we will produce an invalid payload I believe no, but saying that these types of bugs are tricky cause spectests won't cover them even when we add the cases now I am paranoid, having AI scan our code for bunch of stuff, there definitely been a lot of bugs in the past were client reject their own blocks No I used lighthouse and geth https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10300 I have a branch with Justin's PR implemented, passing the new spec test of that PR I found a few bugs on Prysm already due to this, they are unrelated but they are all in the form of "what happens if two slashings come in for the same validator"? All in minor places. One funny one is the rewards API that processes slashings in the wrong order Block production is what I'm covering the most cause a slashing can poisson the pool of the whole fleet so it's more important than STF for liveness But it seems we're clear having stale data in the pool and not re-validating all or most conditions is problematic, eg. https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10217 (also reported by <@1557217203034521660>) I believe prysm is fine, you always re-validate signatures which imo is bad perf wise but least error prone `nflaig/lodestar:clear-builder-payments-on-slash` in case you can easily swap out lighthouse with lodestar Ill give it a try now but it might take me some time. <@586161934425128960> I tested nflaig/lodestar:clear-builder-payments-on-slash with the 5 node test. The builder saw A first; the honest validators saw the self-slashing B first, and B finalized without a payload. B carried a positive 0.101 ETH bid, but all five Lodestar nodes cleared its pending payment, and no corresponding withdrawal occurred at settlement. Your fix prevented the payment-loss path. <@592004585506340885> this requires a spec release, do we aim to have it in hoodi releases? we probably should We were bitten so many times by bugs like this Yes. I would like to wait until Monday if possible. But we can make a release sooner if necessary. cc <@&1417820113981145228> we wanna cut an rc for hoodi tomorrow Okay. We will make a release today. need all focil devnet stuff too? Nah, just going to keep what's in there currently. 8015+8365, no 8198. We can make another release next week if we decide to include 8198. Releases are cheap/easy these days 🙂 Hey <@654267572107083777> could you review the PR? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5719 (haha I'm loving the whip reaction <@586161934425128960>) looking I want Heze releases not tied to Gloas ones. I have some other changes in mind so I want Heze releases have its own cadence. typically, as one hardfork nears/reaches shipping, what drives the releases is the next hardfork, so... but I will specifically say I do _not_ want a special set of "FOCIL" spec releases, insofar as they become a distinct set of things to download and run which have to be reconciled with the "Gloas" ones. There's one set of consensus specs And Nimbus targets that Also consider that we still run all the Altair, Bellatrix, etc etc tests too. There's nothing special about Heze (there's no separate "FOCIL" anymore) There are people already working on Heze. focil-devnet having to wait for Glamsterdam release will slow it down. The point is there's no "Glamsterdam release" or "Heze release" Why you do not want a release for focil-devnet when Nimbus doesn't even have Heze implementation? there's just a consensus-specs release Incidentally, Nimbus has been passing all Heze test vectors for a while now, since they appeared but that's not really the point, it's that there's no separate "Heze" spec. There's a consensus spec be ready for fireworks on the next release <@654267572107083777> so what do you think about that PR? 😅 Remember what thread we're in lol And maybe move this heze stuff elsewhere. I meant a release that will be a target for a specific focil-devnet. I'm kinda speechless about this lol. I would appreciate eyes on this from <@&836981489430036500> & <@&595683849225240704> too. Currently, my plan is to merge this PR and make a release if the Hoodi Glamsterdam upgrade is scheduled at ACDE here in a bit. LGTM

excerpts.author: blueiridium.
excerpts.content: <@586161934425128960> I tested nflaig/lodestar:clear-builder-payments-on-slash with the 5 node test.
